artworks.title: Tomb of Antenor, Padua
artworks.description: Padua's Tomba di Antenore — the shrine that claims the Trojan counselor as the city's founder. Homeric prudence becomes Italian foundation myth: Antenor who urged Helen's return sails on as Padua's first father.

artworks.title: Tomba di Antenore
artworks.description: Another view of the Antenor tomb in Padua: stone and legend binding the Iliad's peace-speaker to the Veneto — not the Athenian sculptor Antenor of the Kore, but Priam's elder.

artworks.title: Antenor (Prato della Valle, Padua)
artworks.description: Statue of Antenor among Padua's Prato della Valle worthies — the Trojan hero still named as civic ancestor centuries after Homer seated him at the Scaean Gate.
